title: reconcile-stream-retry-idempotency-for-tool-calls-and-refine-retry-after-behavior
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Customers integrating streaming tool/function calls through the OpenAI-compat adapter observed surprising retries and duplicate tool invocations when a 429 or transient network error occurred mid-stream. This PR reconciles idempotency usage during streaming tool frames and clarifies/normalizes Retry-After behavior so clients and gateway routing can make deterministic retry decisions. Summary of changes: 1) Introduced an explicit `x-redwood-stream-retry` envelope for gateway->runtime that carries the canonical retry-after expiry (RFC-7231 seconds or absolute RFC3339) and a conflict-tolerant idempotency token derived from the client's idempotency key plus the tool-call frame id. 2) On the OpenAI-compat shim we now map OpenAI-style 429 bodies and Retry-After headers into the canonical envelope instead of emitting ambiguous 429s mid-stream; streaming frames that include function/tool call boundaries will surface `final_frame=true` so downstream can decide whether the tool was invoked. 3) The runtime now treats stream interruption vs final error differently: if the stream was interrupted before a tool-call boundary, a retry is allowed only if the canonical envelope indicates a retry window and the reconciled idempotency token is present; otherwise the request is marked non-idempotent and clients receive a deterministic 409 with guidance. 4) Added compatibility fallbacks: when interacting with older agents that don't understand the envelope, we fall back to best-effort backoff but annotate logs and metrics so SRE can triage. Migration and compatibility notes: No changes required for most SDK consumers; however advanced users who manage their own gateway must start honoring `x-redwood-stream-retry` when present. The OpenAI-compat layer emits the envelope for all responses that could affect tool-call idempotency; older adapters will continue to behave as before but will be accompanied by an advisory header. Testing and verification: unit tests for envelope serialization, integration tests simulating mid-stream 429s and connection drops, and an end-to-end smoke test against a mock tool server verifying single vs duplicate invocations. We also ran a staged rollout to Canary (1% -> 25% -> 100%) while monitoring "duplicate_tool_calls" and "stream_retry_decisions" metrics. Rollout notes: feature gated by `runtime.stream_retry_envelope` for private deployments and toggled via feature flag for hosted. Related work: builds on earlier work to normalize rate-limit headers (see ENG-1888) but diverges by introducing an explicit streaming envelope to avoid ambiguous mid-stream semantics.

review_thread: Arjun Rao: Can we avoid a second idempotency token derivation step in the gateway? It adds CPU in the hot path.

release_notes: Introduces a canonical streaming retry envelope (x-redwood-stream-retry) that clarifies Retry-After semantics and reconciles idempotency tokens at tool-call boundaries. This reduces duplicate tool invocations after mid-stream failures. Backward compatible fallbacks are provided; see docs/api/retry-envelopes.md for migration guidance.
notes_for_ops: Watch metrics duplicate_tool_calls, stream_retry_decisions, and stream_retry_window_misses during rollout. Feature gated — if behavioral regressions appear, toggle runtime.stream_retry_envelope to false to revert to previous behavior.
